versions.text: Standard: Execution of documented crewmember procedures in the flight manuals results in the intended function of the air system for its operational usage. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination. (1) Preparation and review of preliminary flight manuals, modification flight manuals, crewmember checklists, and ancillary flight test documentation (e.g., flight clearance, test operating limitations, engineering source data, test cards) includes affirmation of readiness to begin flight test. (2) Flight manuals reflect the current configuration, operational usage, and operating environment for the air system. (3) Normal procedures in flight manuals and crewmember checklists describe the clear and precise step-by-step actions that the crewmembers need to take to result in the intended function of the air system for its operational usage. (4) Emergency procedures in flight manuals and crewmember checklists describe the clear and precise step-by-step actions that the crewmembers need to take after a non-normal operation or system condition occurs. Test. (1) Lab test: Execution of crewmember procedures, utilizing the flight manuals, crewmember checklists, and ancillary flight test documentation (e.g., flight clearance, test operating limitations, engineering source data, test cards) in a representative environment, results in the intended function of the air system. Crewmember procedures address planned flight test conditions as well as potential emergency situations. (2) Lab test: Execution of procedural mitigations identified through safety analyses verifies mitigation of hazards. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Examination. (5) The flight manuals and crewmember checklists include any procedural mitigations identified by safety analyses and hazards. (6) The flight manuals and crewmember checklists incorporate any necessary revisions identified during testing and documented in the flight test technical report(s). Test. (3) Flight or Ground test: Execution of crewmember procedures, utilizing the preliminary flight manuals, modification flight manuals, crewmember checklists, and ancillary flight test documentation (e.g., flight clearance, operating limitations, engineering source data, test cards), results in the intended function of the air system. (4) Flight, Ground, or Lab test: Execution of procedural mitigations and procedural revisions identified during testing verifies mitigation of hazards and confirms accuracy of the flight manuals.
